thread:
yuki: trying to run our integration test flow inside a Docker container: I mount ~/.config/redwood into the container and run `redwoodctl localserve --port 7000` as app user (uid 1001). localserve starts but `redwoodctl login --device-code` in the container immediately prints `authorization failed, retrying` and then 'device flow expired'. host browser shows success.

yuki: digging into container logs I see: `failed to write profiles.json: open /home/app/.config/redwood/profiles.json: permission denied` even though the file is present and writable on the host. `ls -l` in container shows owner root:root, mode 600.

omar: likely a uid/gid mismatch between host and container mount. Docker bind mounts keep host ownership; if host file was created by root during build, container user won't be able to write. Quick test: `sudo chown 1001:1001 ~/.config/redwood -R` on host or change mount to a tmpfs in CI. Also check clock: container time sometimes lags a few seconds -> device code can expire. run `date` inside container and compare to host.

yuki: `date` inside container is 2024-12-01T02:12:01Z, host is 2024-12-01T02:12:10Z (9s behind). Could that matter?

omar: yes. our auth server rejects device exchanges if token issued_at + skew < now by > 5s in some configs. Fix by syncing clock or not mounting /etc/localtime weirdly in container. But first fix permissions because write error explains the parse/lock issue.

yuki: changed ownership to uid 1001 and re-ran. Now login goes to browser but CLI still retries with `401 invalid_grant` in container logs. Trace shows `profiles.json` contains a stale token plus a `.lock` file was left by the host process (owner root). The container process couldn't atomically replace profiles.json because of EEXIST on rename.

ci-bot: Note: CI pattern using a host-mounted ~/.config is fragile. Recommended: in CI containers, set `REDWOODCTL_CONFIG=/tmp/redwood/profiles.json` and mount an ephemeral tmp dir. Ticket DX-5201 opened for CI docs.

leo: two more things we've seen: 1) proxies in CI (corporate TLS MITM) can rewrite the device flow redirect and cause `invalid_grant`; check `HTTPS_PROXY` and intercepting proxies. 2) If the localserve binds only to 127.0.0.1 inside container, host browser can't reach the callback if you attempt a callback URL. Use device code flow to paste code.

yuki: in my case there was a proxy set in environment inside container that the test harness injected; unsetting `HTTPS_PROXY` allowed token exchange to succeed once ownership fixed and the clock was in sync. I ended up: chown host mount -> use `--device-code` and paste code into the host browser -> unset proxy in container for auth -> set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG to /tmp during CI. Then localserve started and tests could hit 0.0.0.0:7000 with port forwarding.

omar: thanks for the postmortem. small CLI DX ideas: 1) on write errors, print the owning uid/gid and suggest `chown` recovery or offer `--take-lock` interactive option; 2) when a device flow 401 occurs, print likely causes: clock skew, proxy/MITM, corrupted profiles.json, stale lock; 3) detect when running in containers (presence of /.dockerenv) and prefer writable tmp path unless REDWOODCTL_CONFIG is set.

devex-bot: Created DX-5201 "CI/container guidance for redwoodctl config, device flow, and mounts". Suggested changes: detect mount ownership mismatch and surface helpful recovery, document REDWOODCTL_CONFIG usage for CI, and add a non-interactive login token export for ephemeral runners.

leo: follow-up: adding `redwoodctl login --raw-token` (prints token after successful login) would help non-interactive CI flows; or support `--out /tmp/token.json` for runners. I'll propose it in the CLI repo.

yuki: one more note: sample-app expects a unix socket at `/tmp/redwood.sock` but inside container localserve created `/home/app/.run/redwood.sock`; adding `REDWOODCTL_RUN_DIR` env handling in sample-app fixed it. Will attach the mount logs to DX-5201.

yuki: thanks all, happy to share the CI job diff if anyone wants to reuse it. saved me a couple hours. :coffee:
